title: How to Read the New Testament in the Order of the Story
key_points: John 1 opens the plan, showing the Word who was with God before Bethlehem.
Luke and Acts are one story in two volumes, one written, the other continued by the Holy Ghost.
Epistles are placed at the point in Acts where each was actually written and read.
The plan ends with Luke's genealogy climbing backward to Adam, the son of God.

verse.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

scene.caption: In the beginning was the Word
scene.alt: A scroll rests on a path at dawn, light rays breaking over distant hills.

title: The Gospel According to Luke: The Lord Jesus Christ From Bethlehem to the Ascension
key_points: Luke moves from the temple and manger through Galilee toward Jerusalem and the cross.
At Luke 9:51 He steadfastly sets His face to go to Jerusalem, turning the whole book.
The travel narrative carries the good Samaritan, the prodigal son, and Zacchaeus.
The Gospel closes with the ascension, hands lifted in blessing and a church full of joy.

verse.text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.

scene.caption: The road set steadfastly toward Jerusalem
scene.alt: A star shines over rolling hills with a path leading toward distant mountains.

title: The Acts of the Apostles and the Epistles in Their Places
key_points: The risen Lord commands the disciples to wait, then promises power from the Holy Ghost.
Pentecost brings the Spirit and three thousand souls through Peter's preaching.
Saul the persecutor is struck down on the Damascus road and becomes the chief apostle.
Each epistle answers a real crisis at the place in Acts where it was written.

verse.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

scene.caption: Power to be witnesses to the uttermost part of the earth
scene.alt: A flame rests before a distant city, with a trumpet and scroll nearby on open ground.

title: Revelation and the End of the Story
key_points: Revelation opens with a blessing on the reader and the Lord among the seven candlesticks.
The Lamb as it had been slain alone is worthy to open the sealed book.
Babylon falls, and a voice calls the saints to come out of her.
The book ends with a new heaven and new earth where God wipes away every tear.

verse.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

scene.caption: Behold, I make all things new
scene.alt: A holy city glows at dawn above a crown, with a dove flying in the light.
